census.storage: out of Git: over the 204800-byte blob cap of scripts/hygiene/check.py (H145/H44); bound here by size and sha256

criteria.rule: H490 declaration-level verdicts (keep, ownerNeeded, orphan, unresolved) of Solidity.Goals.Inventory, family verdict = classify.family_verdict (keep, else unresolved, else ownerNeeded, else orphan); unchanged

scope.grouping_rule: A module D/XControls.lean or D/XPins.lean, and D/X.lean when either exists, form the family triple:D/X with roles controls, pins and member; D/Controls.lean and D/Pins.lean are the controls/pins of the directory family dir:D/; every other in-scope module belongs to dir:D/ of its own directory (not recursive).
scope.identity: a declaration is a kernel constant with a declaration range; auxiliary constants fold into their nearest ranged name prefix (uses folded alike); module@line is an anonymous check inside the areas (a Controls/Pins one is a demand seed)

limitations: The kernel theorem Solidity.LeanInventory.inventory_sound certifies only the abstract certificate reasoning of Solidity.Goals.Inventory; it does not certify this Python extraction or its completeness, any elapsed time, Git recovery, or deletion safety.
Adequate (every actual use recorded or covered by a listed gap) is an external input obligation of the real census and is not established by any proof or by this tool.

Edges are kernel-term constants of elaborated declarations (types, values, inductive, constructor and recursor links), implemented_by targets, and project names quoted in metaprogram values; elaborator-time uses (tactics, macros, elaborators, instance and simp-set lookups by commands that leave no constant) are not edges and are represented by the implicit-use gaps.
Uses by anonymous commands (example, #guard, #eval, ...) are the explicit identifier references Lean records in .ilean files; their implicit uses are covered by the implicit-use gaps, not observed.

Lean files outside the built libraries (tests/, Bridge/, scripts/, docs/, vscode/, web/) and Lean text generated by runner scripts are not elaborated; their possible uses are gaps bounded by the exact import closure of their headers or of the import lines found in runner text (a dynamic import name is bounded by its static prefix). Runner text that builds an import from data without a static prefix is not detected.
Grouping, command classification, attribute detection and runner import detection are lexical; they only bound gaps or propose candidates and never establish a use or absence.

Check times are Lake job times of one incremental build resumed over several runs on a 4-core VM with parallel jobs (see timing.provenance); modules fetched from the Lake artifact cache have no measured time.

Name references inside scope commands (open, export, variable, attribute [local ...], set_option ... in) and proof-script names that leave no kernel constant (simp only [X]) are not use edges; such a reference can keep a module building without making it a consumer. They are listed for orphan families as dependents, from .ilean name mentions in any position.

unresolved is the conservative verdict: it is precise only as far as the listed gaps; certified orphan families are deletion candidates only, not deletion evidence. An orphan family whose dependents are not empty cannot be deleted alone: its dependents (Lean importers and name mentions in other families, whose uses are themselves orphan, and non-Lean files outside docs/ naming its paths or modules) must be edited or removed in the same change; standalone marks a family with none.

recovery.command: git show 869819299a4ecab7daecacde662634fec93f2cad:PATH  (PATH: any member path below)

authorization.grant: Deleting certified orphan families is authorized (blanket) with recovery pins and unchanged gates.
authorization.covers: exactly the families in `orphans` below, at their recovery pin
conditions: Delete a whole family: its member modules (and controls/pins) together.

A family whose dependents are not empty cannot be deleted alone: in the same change remove or refactor each dependent (Lean importers and name mentions, and non-Lean files outside docs/ naming its paths or modules); standalone families have none.
Re-check against the census at the step's own merge base: a family whose verdict is no longer orphan there is not covered.
keep, ownerNeeded and unresolved families are not covered; unresolved stays excluded until its gaps are closed.
No statement, budget, gate or criterion changes; gates must pass unchanged.
Certified orphan means a deletion candidate under the recorded facts, not deletion evidence: the kernel theorem certifies only the abstract certificate reasoning.
